corruption_model_default: two online parties P0 (model owner) and P1 (client), one static passive corruption of one online party, an independent trusted offline dealer that colludes with nobody, secure authenticated channels
note: One entry per ADMITTED component (plus the TEST_ONLY toy bridge for reference). A ledger entry binds a construction, a paper reference, parameters, the corruption model, the setup, the concurrency scope, a failure bound and test ids. It records obligations and evidence; it is not a self-certification, and hashing an entry binds its version, not its correctness. Statistical or approximation bounds hold on the declared contract domains only.

PL-share_input.construction: Additive secret sharing over Z_2^64: the owner samples s0 uniformly, sends s1 = x - s0 to the other party (one message of public shape).
PL-share_input.reference: Standard additive sharing (information-theoretic); paper, Section 2.2, sharing and products
PL-share_input.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer not involved

PL-linear_wmask.construction: Weight-masked Beaver product: per matrix a reusable dealer mask B (shared) and the public E = W - B revealed once at install (P1 sends B1, P0 returns E = W - B0 - B1); per call fresh (A, C = A B) from the dealer; the parties open X - A and compute Z = C + D [B] + [A] E + D E. Output truncated with trunc_local (contract-bounded operands).
PL-linear_wmask.reference: Beaver, Efficient multiparty protocols using circuit randomization, CRYPTO 1991; multi-use mask argument: each call opens only X_t - A_t with a fresh A_t, so the joint view (E, {X_t - A_t}) is uniform and independent of W and X; versioning of E by (model_version, client_key_domain), never reused across model versions
PL-linear_wmask.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-linear_wmask.setup: trusted dealer bundles (wmask_mask material); installed object version bound to the session
PL-linear_wmask.failure_bound: truncation: a locally truncated value x is off by a full wrap of 2^(64-s) ring units with probability |x|/2^64 (SecureML local truncation); a 4-layer session of 16 prompt and 8 generated tokens executes 5.49 million local truncations and a 12-layer session 15.6 million; the sum over the truncations that can reach a released token gives a wrong token sequence in about 0.8 percent (4 layers) and 2.4 percent (12 layers) of sessions; a wrap in the LM head is harmless because the argmax compares modulo 2^32

PL-linear_generic.construction: Beaver matrix product with a weight-independent matrix triple (A, B, C = A B); W is shared in by P0; the parties open X - A and W - B.
PL-linear_generic.reference: Beaver, CRYPTO 1991; matrix-triple form as in SecureML (Mohassel and Zhang, S&P 2017)
PL-linear_generic.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-linear_generic.failure_bound: truncation: a locally truncated value x is off by a full wrap of 2^(64-s) ring units with probability |x|/2^64 (SecureML local truncation); per session see PL-trunc_local

PL-embedding_wmask.construction: linear_wmask applied to the client's shared one-hot row (n = 1, d_in = V, d_out = d_model); no truncation (the one-hot is exact).
PL-embedding_wmask.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-embedding_wmask.setup: installed object wte at the session version

PL-embedding_generic.construction: linear_generic applied to the client's shared one-hot row; no truncation; no installed object.
PL-embedding_generic.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer

PL-matmul_shared.construction: Beaver matrix product of two shared operands with a matrix triple; used for Q K^T and P V.
PL-matmul_shared.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-matmul_shared.failure_bound: truncation: a locally truncated value x is off by a full wrap of 2^(64-s) ring units with probability |x|/2^64 (SecureML local truncation); per session see PL-trunc_local

PL-drelu.construction: One-round DReLU: open y = x + r; with p = r mod 2^n and q = (r + 2^(n-1)) mod 2^n, 1{x >= 0} = DCF_q(y_n) - DCF_p(y_n) + 1{p > q}; the dealer ships shares of r, 1{p > q} and 1{p > q} r.
PL-drelu.reference: Boyle, Chandran, Gilboa, Gupta, Ishai, Kumar, Rathee, Function secret sharing for mixed-mode and fixed-point secure computation, Eurocrypt 2021 (DCF); product-group Convert of Boyle, Chandran, Gilboa, Gupta, Ishai, Kumar, Rathee (Function secret sharing for mixed-mode and fixed-point secure computation, Eurocrypt 2021): every payload component is converted with its own pseudo-random words (paper, Section 5.3, a finding on comparison keys); paper, Section 5.3, one-round DReLU
PL-drelu.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer generates the DCF keys
PL-drelu.setup: fixed-key AES PRG (Matyas-Meyer-Oseas) for the GGM tree with component-specific value words (tweaks 2 and 4, 5, ... over Z_2^64); one-time keys
PL-drelu.failure_bound: 0 (exact) given |x| < 2^(n-1) ring units; keys are one-time (reuse is a ledger error)

PL-relu.construction: drelu with payload (1, r): ReLU(x) = y [b] - [r b] in the same round; the two payload components use independent Convert words, so a key reveals neither alpha = r mod 2^n nor beta_1 - beta_0.
PL-relu.reference: as PL-drelu (payload P = 2); product-group Convert of Boyle, Chandran, Gilboa, Gupta, Ishai, Kumar, Rathee (Function secret sharing for mixed-mode and fixed-point secure computation, Eurocrypt 2021): every payload component is converted with its own pseudo-random words (paper, Section 5.3, a finding on comparison keys); the single-word rule of the superseded engine leaked the mask r from one key and is not used
PL-relu.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer

PL-trunc_faithful.construction: Faithful truncation gate with the signed offset: P0 adds a = 2^(L-1); open y = x' + r; [w] = DCF_A(y) (wrap), [b] = DCF_B(y mod 2^f) (borrow); [z] = floor(y/2^f) 1{P0} - [floor(r/2^f)] - [b] + 2^(64-f) [w] - 2^(L-1-f) 1{P0}.
PL-trunc_faithful.reference: paper, Section 5.1, faithful truncation; regression k = 8, L = 6, f = 3, x = -13, r = 37 must give -2 (the printed formula without the last term gives 2); DCF as in PL-drelu
PL-trunc_faithful.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-trunc_faithful.setup: trusted dealer bundles (trunc_faithful material): r, floor(r/2^f), 64-bit wrap key, f-bit borrow key
PL-trunc_faithful.failure_bound: 0 (exact) for x in [-2^(L-1), 2^(L-1)); privacy: y is uniform and independent of x for uniform r; w and b never opened

PL-trunc_local.construction: SecureML local probabilistic truncation: each party shifts its own share (P1 negates, shifts, negates); zero rounds, no material.
PL-trunc_local.reference: Mohassel and Zhang, SecureML, IEEE S&P 2017, Theorem 1
PL-trunc_local.failure_bound: a locally truncated value x is off by a full wrap of 2^(64-s) ring units with probability |x|/2^64 (SecureML local truncation); a 4-layer session of 16 prompt and 8 generated tokens executes 5.49 million local truncations and a 12-layer session 15.6 million; the sum over the truncations that can reach a released token gives a wrong token sequence in about 0.8 percent (4 layers) and 2.4 percent (12 layers) of sessions; a wrap in the LM head is harmless because the argmax compares modulo 2^32; the LayerNorm square is excluded (uses trunc_faithful)

PL-softmax_rows_k2.construction: Row max by a binary tournament (one DReLU and one Beaver select per pair, 2 rounds per level), z = x - max, exp_neg(z) with clamp at -16, order-2 base and 7 squarings at scale 2^(f+4), S = sum t (local), recip(S) with K = 11 threshold DReLUs, degree-5 polynomial and 2 Newton steps, out = t * recip. Causal and padding masks are public.
PL-softmax_rows_k2.reference: paper, Section 5.4, operators composed from the blocks; comparisons by PL-drelu (DCF with the product-group Convert of Boyle, Chandran, Gilboa, Gupta, Ishai, Kumar, Rathee (Function secret sharing for mixed-mode and fixed-point secure computation, Eurocrypt 2021): every payload component is converted with its own pseudo-random words (paper, Section 5.3, a finding on comparison keys)); products by PL-matmul_shared/Beaver; approximation contracts in approx.py
PL-softmax_rows_k2.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-softmax_rows_k2.setup: trusted dealer bundles (drelu, beaver, kary_select material)
PL-softmax_rows_k2.failure_bound: max: 0 (exact) given compared differences below 2^(n-2-ceil(log2 g)) ring units inside every node of g >= 3 members and below 2^(n-1) for nodes of two members and pairwise comparisons; the bound is checked at admission from the numeric contract (n, f) and the declared public operand bound of the site (registry.admit: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, detail KARY_MAGNITUDE), never from secret values; exp and recip polynomial approximation errors per contract; products truncated with trunc_local (off by 2^(64-s) with probability |x|/2^64 per element; per session see PL-trunc_local)

PL-softmax_rows_k4.construction: As PL-softmax_rows_k2 with a fused 4-ary max tournament (2 ceil(log4 T) rounds): per level the survivors are grouped into nodes of at most k; round 1: g(g-1)/2 pairwise DReLUs without payload per node of g members, ranks computed locally; round 2: one Beaver select per output value for a node of two members, g-1 DReLUs with the product payload per output value for a node of g >= 3 members (u_i = (rank_i - (g-1)) M + (x_i - x_0) + M/2, M = 2^(n-1-ceil(log2 g))); identical output.
PL-softmax_rows_k4.reference: as PL-softmax_rows_k2; the payload DReLUs of the fused nodes are P = 2 keys under the product-group Convert of Boyle, Chandran, Gilboa, Gupta, Ishai, Kumar, Rathee (Function secret sharing for mixed-mode and fixed-point secure computation, Eurocrypt 2021): every payload component is converted with its own pseudo-random words (paper, Section 5.3, a finding on comparison keys)
PL-softmax_rows_k4.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-softmax_rows_k4.failure_bound: max: 0 (exact) given compared differences below 2^(n-2-ceil(log2 g)) ring units inside every node of g >= 3 members and below 2^(n-1) for nodes of two members and pairwise comparisons; the bound is checked at admission from the numeric contract (n, f) and the declared public operand bound of the site (registry.admit: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, detail KARY_MAGNITUDE), never from secret values; otherwise as PL-softmax_rows_k2

PL-layernorm_rows.construction: mu = mean(x) (local, public 1/d), dx = x - mu, var = mean(dx*dx) with the square truncated by trunc_faithful (exact), rs = rsqrt(var + eps) with j0 = -7, m = 15 threshold DReLUs, degree-5 polynomial and 2 Newton steps, y = dx * rs, out = y * gamma + beta (gamma, beta shared by the dealer).
PL-layernorm_rows.reference: paper, Section 5.4, operators composed from the blocks; PL-trunc_faithful for the square
PL-layernorm_rows.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-layernorm_rows.setup: trusted dealer bundles (beaver, trunc_faithful, drelu, vector_share material)
PL-layernorm_rows.failure_bound: square exact; rsqrt normalisation product V * s2 is a 34-bit value (s2 at scale 2^(f+e2), e2 = max(0, 2 (j0+1+m) - f) = 2): <= 2^-29 per row; remaining products off by 2^(64-s) with probability |x|/2^64 per element (trunc_local, per session see PL-trunc_local); rsqrt approximation error per contract

PL-gelu_clip12.construction: Clip at |x| <= R = 5 with two DReLUs, degree-12 polynomial (Chebyshev-node least squares of erf-GELU on [-5, 5]) by Horner in fixed point, blend with the clipped linear parts.
PL-gelu_clip12.reference: paper, Section 5.4, operators composed from the blocks; approx.py contract gelu_clip12 (max_abs_err 4.84e-3); erf-GELU semantics disclosed (not gelu_new)
PL-gelu_clip12.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-gelu_clip12.failure_bound: approximation max_abs_err 4.84e-3 on the contract domain (not a failure probability); products truncated with trunc_local (off by 2^(64-s) with probability |x|/2^64 per element; per session see PL-trunc_local)

PL-silu_clip12.construction: Clip at |x| <= R = 8 with two DReLUs, degree-12 polynomial by Horner, blend.
PL-silu_clip12.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-silu_clip12.failure_bound: approximation error per contract silu_clip12; products truncated with trunc_local (off by 2^(64-s) with probability |x|/2^64 per element; per session see PL-trunc_local)

PL-argmax_k2.construction: Binary tournament over the V logits: b = DReLU(a - b'), keep b a + (1 - b) b' and the index b i + (1 - b) i' (ring elements, one Beaver select per output value; the index select is local on the first level where indices are public); lowest index wins ties; the final index shares are released only through release_final.
PL-argmax_k2.reference: paper, Section 5.3, equivalent k-ary selection realizations; comparisons by PL-drelu (DCF with the product-group Convert of Boyle, Chandran, Gilboa, Gupta, Ishai, Kumar, Rathee (Function secret sharing for mixed-mode and fixed-point secure computation, Eurocrypt 2021): every payload component is converted with its own pseudo-random words (paper, Section 5.3, a finding on comparison keys)); selects by Beaver products
PL-argmax_k2.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-argmax_k2.failure_bound: 0 (exact) given compared differences below 2^(n-2-ceil(log2 g)) ring units inside every node of g >= 3 members and below 2^(n-1) for nodes of two members and pairwise comparisons; the bound is checked at admission from the numeric contract (n, f) and the declared public operand bound of the site (registry.admit: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, detail KARY_MAGNITUDE), never from secret values

PL-argmax_k4.construction: Fused 4-ary tournament (2 ceil(log4 V) rounds): per level the survivors are grouped into nodes of at most k; round 1: g(g-1)/2 pairwise DReLUs without payload per node of g members, ranks computed locally; round 2: one Beaver select per output value for a node of two members, g-1 DReLUs with the product payload per output value for a node of g >= 3 members (u_i = (rank_i - (g-1)) M + (x_i - x_0) + M/2, M = 2^(n-1-ceil(log2 g))); the index is an output value on every level after the first; output identical to argmax_k2 (lowest index on ties).
PL-argmax_k4.reference: as PL-argmax_k2; the payload DReLUs of the fused nodes are P = 2 keys under the product-group Convert of Boyle, Chandran, Gilboa, Gupta, Ishai, Kumar, Rathee (Function secret sharing for mixed-mode and fixed-point secure computation, Eurocrypt 2021): every payload component is converted with its own pseudo-random words (paper, Section 5.3, a finding on comparison keys)
PL-argmax_k4.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-argmax_k4.failure_bound: 0 (exact) given compared differences below 2^(n-2-ceil(log2 g)) ring units inside every node of g >= 3 members and below 2^(n-1) for nodes of two members and pairwise comparisons; the bound is checked at admission from the numeric contract (n, f) and the declared public operand bound of the site (registry.admit: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, detail KARY_MAGNITUDE), never from secret values

PL-argmax_k8.construction: Fused 8-ary tournament (2 ceil(log8 V) rounds): per level the survivors are grouped into nodes of at most k; round 1: g(g-1)/2 pairwise DReLUs without payload per node of g members, ranks computed locally; round 2: one Beaver select per output value for a node of two members, g-1 DReLUs with the product payload per output value for a node of g >= 3 members (u_i = (rank_i - (g-1)) M + (x_i - x_0) + M/2, M = 2^(n-1-ceil(log2 g))); the index is an output value on every level after the first; output identical to argmax_k2 (lowest index on ties).
PL-argmax_k8.reference: as PL-argmax_k2; the payload DReLUs of the fused nodes are P = 2 keys under the product-group Convert of Boyle, Chandran, Gilboa, Gupta, Ishai, Kumar, Rathee (Function secret sharing for mixed-mode and fixed-point secure computation, Eurocrypt 2021): every payload component is converted with its own pseudo-random words (paper, Section 5.3, a finding on comparison keys)
PL-argmax_k8.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-argmax_k8.failure_bound: 0 (exact) given compared differences below 2^(n-2-ceil(log2 g)) ring units inside every node of g >= 3 members and below 2^(n-1) for nodes of two members and pairwise comparisons; the bound is checked at admission from the numeric contract (n, f) and the declared public operand bound of the site (registry.admit: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, detail KARY_MAGNITUDE), never from secret values

PL-ring_to_field.construction: A64 -> Zt resharing with signed carry: open y = u + r; [w]_t = DCF_A(y) (wrap), [nn]_t = DCF_C(y) - DCF_A(y) + [c]_t (sign by the DReLU identity with n = 64), [b]_t = 1 - [nn]_t; [u mod t]_t = (y mod t) 1{P0} - [r mod t]_t + (q mod t) [w]_t; [z]_t = [u mod t]_t - (q mod t) [b]_t.
PL-ring_to_field.reference: paper, Section 5.2, exact ring-to-field conversion; counterexample q = 256, t = 17, a0 = 255, a1 = 2 gives 1 (naive share-wise reduction gives 2); DCF with Z_t payload as in PL-drelu, value words are 128-bit PRG blocks reduced mod t (paper, Section 5.3, a finding on comparison keys; Section 6, loss)
PL-ring_to_field.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer
PL-ring_to_field.failure_bound: n_word * t / 2^128 per element (statistical distance of the Z_t key words from uniform), n_word = 516 = 2 key pairs x (4 x 64 level words + 2 leaf words): 2^-82.99 per element at t = 68720050177; charged to the session budget at admission (kappa_sys = 64); the reconstruction itself is exact and nothing but the uniform y is communicated, w and b stay shared

PL-a2h_exact.construction: ring_to_field then BFV: P1 encrypts its Z_t share z1 (batched, plaintext modulus t, N = 8192) under its own key and sends the ciphertext to P0; P0 adds z0 as a plaintext. Exact Enc(z) under P1's key held by P0 only; P1 never sees the ciphertext. Admitted at the primitive level: no admitted component consumes H_BFV (he_linear_bfv_matvec is UNAVAILABLE), so no layer lane exists.
PL-a2h_exact.reference: Brakerski, Fully homomorphic encryption without modulus switching, CRYPTO 2012; Fan and Vercauteren, Somewhat practical FHE, 2012; Microsoft SEAL via TenSEAL 0.3.17; paper, Section 5.2, ExactA2H
PL-a2h_exact.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer for ring_to_field; IND-CPA of BFV against P0
PL-a2h_exact.setup: P1 BFV key generation; P0 receives the public context only
PL-a2h_exact.failure_bound: ring_to_field part: n_word * t / 2^128 per element as PL-ring_to_field; BFV part: 0 (exact) within the noise budget of a plaintext addition; privacy against P0 computational (BFV IND-CPA)

PL-release_final.construction: RELEASE_FINAL: P0 sends its share of the declared output to P1; the ReleasePolicy enforces recipient, type and count and raises UnauthorizedRelease otherwise. No other reveal of a model-derived value exists in secure builds.
PL-release_final.reference: paper, Section 3.2, authorized outputs and public information
PL-release_final.setup: ReleasePolicy declared in the session protocol
PL-release_final.failure_bound: n/a (releases exactly the declared functionality output)

PL-toy_bridge.construction: Toy power-of-two BFV reference bridge: A2H_toy (P1 encrypts its share, P0 adds Delta x0), Eval_toy (plaintext-weight coefficient-encoded matvec), H2A_ref (c1 s by Beaver triples over Z_q, P0 adds c0 + Delta/2 locally, faithful truncation by 64 - m bits). The keyholder never sees ct, c1 s or the noise; P0 never sees s.
PL-toy_bridge.reference: paper, Appendix B, H2A-ref (reference design); coefficient-encoding trick as in Cheetah/Iron
PL-toy_bridge.corruption_model: one static passive online party; trusted dealer for the Beaver triples
PL-toy_bridge.setup: P1 toy BFV keys; parameter sets that violate the noise bound are refused
PL-toy_bridge.failure_bound: 0 within the checked noise bound; toy scheme, no computational security claim on real parameters
